¶9.
** Genuine

 of the natural mind,

 the whole
 of natural

, only
 in certain
 particular states
 within
 the natural mind are
 wis
doms brought
 forth. For
 divine
 love blaz
es from
 above and descends into the natural mind
,
 and where
 it meets the field
 of natural knowledge it
 produces the
 first external appearances of truth —
 as
 when
 celest
ial infl
ux

 out
ward memory
-
knowledge
 and

irs it into

 preliminary
 doctrinal form. Divine
 truth

 the

termost forms;
 and

ified natural truths receive
 it
,
 drawing
 it toward themselves within
 the natural
 mind.


**¶10.** This
 individual
 influx of divine truth descends into
 the purified natural truths and
 is absorbed by
 them, and
 they
 are con
joined.
 The
 infl
ux does not sink
 into the deep
est obsc
ur
ities of merely
 natural knowledge;
 instead
 it
 remains at
 the level
 of conscious awareness, accessible
 within
 the mind
. Around
 this
 whol
esome infl
ux, an
 external doctrinal form takes
 shape —
 first
 as
 a
 preliminary
 appearance
, then as a fir
mer containing
 vessel
 —
 and
 within
 it
,
 a genuine
 wisdom begins
 to crystall
ize.
 Yet
 when
 divine
 truth
 cannot
 be received whole, it breaks apart
 and
 is
 distributed

 lesser
 portions
, each
 requiring
 its
 own time
 of

 made
 good
 and
 recept
ive.
 When
 at

ial truth and

ated within

 the

 — they are

joined with
 one another and are

 precious
 wisdom of
 full
 worth
.

**¶11.**
 When,
 however, an infl
ux of
 divine truth desc
ends and
 that
 infl
ux is
 frag
mented into many
 lesser
 portions and
 various
 scattered
 particles of
 understanding
, these
 are
 formed into and enclosed
 within
 numerous smaller
 wisdoms, each
 held

 doctrinal vessel
. One
 containing

 two wis
doms, another may

 some hold

**¶12.** Now
, when a whole and
 und
ivided influx of
 divine truth is received,
 and
 the containing doc
trinal form receives it intact
, it becomes a great and precious
 wisdom,
 its
 perf
ection complete
. Yet
 even
 if the
 truth
 has
 been
 divided
 into
 lesser
 portions, if these portions have
 time to adhere to one another before
 any
 understanding
 is
 lost, and
 they
 are conjoined with each
 other, and
 the containing form en
closes them before
 they scatter further
 —
 then
 they too may
 be
 shaped into a great wisdom,
 and the
 celest
ial infl
ux together
 with the purified natural tru
ths within
 them
 forms
 a great and valued
 good
.

**¶13.**
 Behold, I have shown
 how
 genuine
 wisdoms are formed within
 the natural mind. I have told you
 that just
 as wisdom
 comes into existence by means of divine
 truth that
 has time to be
 received
 into preliminary
 appearances
, the
 external
 doctrinal form comes into existence by
 means of those
 appearances
, and those
 very
 appearances arise
 from
 the transformation
 and
 the working
 of the natural
 mind itself
 under
 infl
ux.


**¶14.** Then
,
 when
 those
 who possess
 spiritual perception —
 who
 search the depths
 of the natural mind —
 recognize
 the time
,
 they desc
end into
 those
 particular
 states and bring wis
doms up from the obsc
ur
ities of natural
 knowledge into
 the light
.
 Each one
 who searches
 finds
 according to the providence
 that is ordained
 for him
. These
 seek
ers deliver
 what
 they find
 to those
 who transm
it and
 communicate wisdom
,
 and those transmitters deliver
 it in
 turn to the ruling
 loves
 of the will
 and to
 the governing
 principles
 of the understanding
 —
 to whatever
 is
 sovereign
 in the mind
.

**¶17.**
 For all the interior
 aff
ections that
 rise up
 through

 and

eal state

erated from

enly states

, a
 dwelling
-
place within

ial real
ms of the
 Divine
 Great
ness.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: "Pearls shall arise not in every place in the sea, nor be formed in the sea as a whole. Rather, in various places that are in this sea, pearls are formed in them[. Now, in] that sea, in which the [pearls] shall be formed[,] this [is the way of their formation:] what the sea shall [cast forth from] its fire above and comes [down upon the waters,] and it makes foam like the drop of water that flows [from above] down in rainwater[. This] is the water [that comes d]own first [into the] foam and comes down [to] the sweet waters[, and they receive] the waters.

"When, however, a drop of rainwater falls, and that drop breaks into many droplets and various , they shall be formed into and be confined in [n]umerous pearls, in the shell and the pearl-shell. One might form two pearls, another may form three, others may form five; some mould more than these, some fewer.

"Now, when you might [find a] whole drop, and the shell receives it, it shall become a great and valued [pe]arl as its worth is perfected. [However], if these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another before any (water particle) escapes, and they mix with e[ach o]ther, and the shell [encloses them] before they break into [many parts] within [it, and they are shaped] in a great kind[. For] the drop of rain, which [combines with] another one, that [comes forth from] the [w]aters form them in [a pearl, and] in a great, valued commodity.

"Behold, [I, I have] taught you how sea-pearls shall be formed. I have told you that as a pearl shall come into existence by means of rainwater that has [ti]me to become foam, the pearl-shell shall come into existence by means of the foam, and the foam itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [working] of the sea.

"Then immediately at the time when [the pearls are formed,] the pearl divers know it, they shall [come,] and they [go d]own to those places and they bring pearls up from the depths of the sea, and each pearl diver finds according to the fortune that is [ordai]ned for him. The pearl divers shall [gi]ve them to the traders, and the traders give them to the kings and the nobles.

"Fo[r a]ll the souls that ascend in the flesh of mankind and are freed shall be brought back to the great aeons of light. A place of rest comes about for them, at that place in the aeons of greatness.

“This drop of water shall [ ... ] down to the sweet waters and [ ... ] and they absorbed them and were combined with the [ ... ]. They did not [d]escend to the depths of the sea, but they [ ... ... ] it floated on the surface of the waters [ ... ... ] to it. The foam and the pearl-shell shall be formed [ ... ] this wholesome drop [ ... ... ] it, and it becomes a pe[arl ... ] that makes a drop of rainwater [ ... ] waters [ ... ] it not being whole. It breaks and separates out into many droplets, and it has time to become a drop of sweet water [ ... ] and comes up in the sea of [ ... ] rain and sweet water; and it is accomodated in the shell, which at first is foam. They shall be joined with each other at [this] time, and are shaped and become a great pea[r]l, a great and valued kind.
